findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, with confusing dead logic
findings.body: The function computes `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false on both branches. It is unconditionally disabled regardless of the feature flag. That is the intended security fix, but the inverted flag check and the redundant branches look like a bug and mislead readers into thinking the flag still controls the feature. It should be a plain `return false` with a comment explaining why. The error message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' also gives users no hint that the feature was deliberately disabled.

findings.title: SQL expressions are still reachable through the non-reader path
findings.body: Only ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery is gated. UnmarshalSQLCommand in sql_command.go (used by the legacy node-building path) still calls NewSQLCommand, and nothing in that path checks the flag or the disabled state. Because the stub DB returns 'not implemented' from TablesList, those queries fail rather than execute. Still, the disabling is incidental to the stub and not enforced at the entry point. Add an explicit guard in NewSQLCommand or UnmarshalSQLCommand.

findings.title: No tests cover the disabled behaviour
findings.body: The PR changes SQL expression behaviour to always fail but adds no test asserting that QueryTypeSQL returns an error and that the stub DB errors. Any existing SQL expression tests that expect success will now fail or silently go stale.
